stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key ML/AI domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and practical application of Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to study dark matter and dark energy
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been successfully launched after funding and name changes.
It will travel to the L2 Lagrange point beyond the Moon for observation.
The telescope is designed to conduct an unprecedented survey of the universe to study dark matter and dark energy.

stories.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music publishers (Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell) are suing Anthropic.
The lawsuit alleges unauthorized use of tens of thousands of copyrighted musical works by Anthropic.
The plaintiffs are seeking substantial damages, potentially up to $150,000 per work.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
Tags suggest relevance to transformer architectures and conversational AI applications.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in large language model tasks.
The model is associated with key technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the mainstream LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for persistent AI agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool use.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and multi-token prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Macs.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating an ongoing development push for local AI.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that a blacklisting action by Trump against Anthropic was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed the development of lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance technologies.
The story highlights legal challenges surrounding government actions targeting AI companies based on their ethical stances.

stories.title: Real-time virtual circuits for plasma shape control via neural network emulators: experimental demonstration on MAST Upgrade
stories.author: James Buchanan
bullet_points: Presents the first experimental demonstration of real-time virtual circuits (VCs) for plasma shape control in tokamaks.
Replaces traditional offline lookup tables with VCs updated in real time using neural network surrogates of plasma response.
Addresses a critical limitation in conventional plasma control by enabling dynamic, real-time adaptation.

stories.title: Prove2Me: An Open Collaborative Platform for Scaling Math Formalization
stories.author: Tianyi Peng
bullet_points: Introduces Proof2Me, an open collaborative platform designed to scale mathematical formalization.
Addresses major barriers in formal verification (expertise and time) by leveraging AI coding agents.
Enables users to prompt complex proofs in formal systems like Lean 4 using natural language.

stories.title: Program Learning with Verifiable Rewards: Symbolic Backpropagation for Post-Training LLMs
stories.author: Vishvesh Bhat
bullet_points: Proposes 'Program Learning with Verifiable Rewards' (PLVR) for post-training LLMs.
Argues that reasoning steps for verifiable tasks should be externalized as explicit programs rather than embedded in model weights.
Addresses the black-box nature of traditional fine-tuning (SFT/RL) by allowing step-by-step inspection of reasoning.

stories.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
stories.author: Jinyuan Jia
bullet_points: Introduces LongPIBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test prompt injection attacks in long-context settings.
Addresses a critical gap in current research where existing benchmarks only cover short-context inputs, leading to defense overestimation.
Focuses on a major security concern in LLMs—prompt injection—by providing realistic, long-context testing scenarios.

stories.title: Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root
stories.author: 0xcc.io via ucirello
bullet_points: The vulnerability, named Omarchy, allows any user process to escalate privileges to root.
This represents a critical security flaw, indicating a severe potential for system compromise.
The discovery is reported on Lobsters, suggesting it is a technical security disclosure.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically boosting capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Texas Governor Abbott halted state funding for Flock AI surveillance cameras amid growing public backlash.
A Texas Tribune investigation revealed the state had spent over $30 million on the Flock camera system.
The funding for these cameras was primarily generated by imposing a $1 fee on insurance policies.

stories.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
stories.author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Meta is actively piloting the use of robotics within its data center infrastructure.
The robots are being tested on tasks currently performed by human technicians.
This signals a potential shift toward increased automation in large-scale data center operations.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: The study involved submitting data deletion requests to 100 different companies.
The process of requesting data deletion was found to be confusing and often resulted in dead ends.
The findings highlight systemic issues regarding data privacy compliance and user rights enforcement across various corporations.

stories.title: ARC-CT: Anatomy-Routed Contrastive Vision-Language Learning for 3D Chest CT
stories.author: Şeyda Ertekin
bullet_points: Introduces ARC-CT, a new method for Vision-Language Learning specifically for 3D Chest CT analysis.
Addresses limitations of global contrastive learning in medical imaging, where small, localized abnormalities can be diluted by volume pooling.
Proposes an 'Anatomy-Routed' approach to better capture localized visual evidence from CT scans when paired with radiology reports.

stories.title: Learning to Use Tools: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Integrated Mathematical Reasoning
stories.author: Zi Wang
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of LLMs in mathematical reasoning by integrating external tools, specifically a calculator.
Analysis revealed that calculation errors are a major contributor to LLM failures on complex tasks like the Countdown game.
The authors propose using supervised fine-tuning to teach LLMs effective patterns for tool utilization.

stories.title: Fidelity Is Not Enough: Dispatch-Level Instrumentation for Agentic Datasheet Extraction
stories.author: Meng-Hsuan Lin
bullet_points: The paper highlights a critical flaw in current agentic document extraction evaluation, where high fidelity scores can mask fabrication.
A model was found to generate answers without using the necessary tools, succeeding only because the underlying tool use was silently disabled by a structured-output constraint.
The research advocates for logging every tool call (dispatch-level instrumentation) as a necessary step beyond simple output fidelity checks for robust agent evaluation.

stories.title: Are These Modules Worth Their Cost? A Paradigm-Level Accuracy-Cost Analysis of In-context Learning Text-to-SQL
stories.author: Feiran Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current Text-to-SQL research by moving beyond aggregate accuracy reporting.
It proposes a paradigm-level analysis to quantify the marginal accuracy-cost contribution of individual design choices in ICL pipelines.
This work is critical for researchers aiming to optimize and configure complex in-context learning systems.

stories.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents
stories.author: Nan Li
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current AI evaluation by focusing on dynamic, stateful dialogue game environments rather than static benchmarks.

The study identifies that many failures in small language models (2B parameter) in these interactive settings are 'local decision failures' (e.g., repeated guesses, invalid actions) rather than just broad knowledge gaps.
It proposes a 'diagnosis-guided post-training recipe' to improve model performance specifically in complex, turn-based interactive tasks.

stories.title: Sliding-window beats linear attention
stories.author: Emy Gervais
bullet_points: Quadratic attention in LLMs leads to unsustainable memory and energy consumption as token count increases.
The memory bottleneck stems from the need to store keys and values indefinitely for every new token.
Sliding-window mechanisms are presented as a viable alternative to Linear Attention for mitigating quadratic scaling issues in LLMs.

stories.title: Curvature-Conditioned Multiscale Momentum with Sphere Constraints for LLM Pretraining
stories.author: Kun Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses a core challenge in LLM pretraining: the ill-conditioned loss landscape and noise-dominant gradients.
Proposes a novel optimization technique, 'Curvature-Conditioned Multiscale Momentum with Sphere Constraints,' to improve training stability.
Suggests that existing adaptive optimizers (like AdamW) are limited because they do not sufficiently mitigate curvature issues, especially along flat directions.

stories.title: SymboLLM-FE: LLM-Accelerated Symbolic Regression for Automated Feature Engineering on Tabular Data
stories.author: Lan-Zhe Guo
bullet_points: Introduces SymboLLM-FE, a new method combining LLMs with Symbolic Regression for Automated Feature Engineering (AutoFE).
Addresses the limitation of traditional AutoFE, which often produces uninterpretable features through blind mathematical transformations.
Focuses on improving feature informativeness and model performance specifically for tabular data, a common ML data format.

stories.title: Post-Training VLMs for Video Mistake Detection
stories.author: Juergen Gall
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of current video mistake detection methods, which rely on closed-set protocols.
The paper proposes a shift towards more generalizable mistake detection methods that do not require retraining for task changes.
The work focuses on Post-Training Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to improve the robustness of mistake detection in real-world video scenarios.

stories.title: Quantum Federated Learning Based on Bures--Uhlmann Geometry for Heterogeneous Noisy Clients
stories.author: Yuuki Tokunaga
bullet_points: The research addresses challenges in Quantum Federated Learning (QFL) for heterogeneous and noisy quantum devices.
It introduces an extension of parameter-space geometry to account for mixed states, which are characteristic of noisy clients.
The work aims to overcome limitations of previous pure-state and diagonal approximation methods by preserving parameter incompatibility correlations.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to enhance LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) used to improve LLM performance.
Leverages the insight that LLM failure modes follow structured patterns across different model scales within the same family.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences into reusable skills.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories, hindering systematic reuse.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by persistently storing and reusing learned skills.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the issue of noisy supervision when training LLMs for real-world software problem-solving.
Prior methods relied on large-scale agent trajectory datasets from successful tasks, which can still contain suboptimal steps.
SWE-Prime proposes a method to improve LLM performance by reducing the number of necessary trajectories while enhancing supervision quality.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in current LLM post-training methods like RL and OPSD.
Existing methods rely on ground-truth labels, which prevents effective test-time training (TTT).
TTPO proposes using majority-vote pseudo-labels as an alternative to ground truth, while analyzing the fragility and asymmetry of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a more realistic, multi-round, and interactive manner.
The research aims to capture the complex, iterative problem-solving nature of real-world software development code reviews.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a known issue in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) where LLM policy entropy collapses, limiting reasoning coverage.
The proposed method introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR training.
This work aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities while mitigating the degradation of pass@$k$ scores associated with entropy collapse.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize complex moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to geometrically analyze the relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical deployment issue in clinical NLP: models overfit to note-specific artifacts rather than true patient state.
Introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework for improving model robustness and auditability.
Uses Sparse Autoencoders to extract human-auditable features from Transformer activations to guide fine-tuning.

stories.title: Native CORS support on GKE Gateway: Offloading cross-origin policy management to infrastructure
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: GKE Gateway now offers native CORS support, shifting cross-origin policy management to the infrastructure layer.
This feature offloads the handling of CORS preflight requests and header injection to Google Cloud Load Balancing.
It represents an infrastructure improvement for Kubernetes deployments, simplifying application configuration for cross-origin requests.

stories.title: I gave an AI agent a production rollback button — then spent the hackathon trying to trick it into pressing it
stories.author: prince_panchani_f971a20ec
bullet_points: The article explores the vulnerability of AI agents, specifically when critical safety mechanisms like rollback buttons are implemented.
A minor configuration error (a one-line omission) in a tool definition can bypass an AI agent's approval gate.
The narrative highlights the risks of trusting AI agents without rigorous security testing, even in controlled environments like hackathons.

stories.title: Running Coding Agents in Parallel with Git Worktrees
stories.author: servatj
bullet_points: Proposes running multiple AI coding agents concurrently within a single repository.
Leverages Git worktrees as the mechanism to isolate and manage parallel agent operations.
Simplifies the integration and finalization process by relying on standard Git merging.
